course_description:
This course enables students to elevate their existing scientific communication skillsets, directly supporting the presentation of original research both in written and oral presentations. Students will be trained in critical, creative and practical thinking, communicating with expert and lay audiences, project management and data analysis.

Lab coat, tick, safety glasses, tick, licence to perform experiments, tick….. What am I missing?

Being a highly skilled and successful biomedical researcher in today’s world requires far more than scientific knowledge and laboratory skills. You need to be able to (1) identify reliable resources, (2) design appropriate experiments, (3) critique the work of others, (4) effectively communicate to diverse audiences and (5) build collegial and sustainable networks.

In BIOM6070 you will work individually and collaboratively with your peers under the guidance of experienced UQ biomedical researchers. The format for this course includes pre-reading, a series of focused interactive workshops and the delivery of small and large assignments that are designed to support your preparation for Honours and future study/careers.

By the end of this course, you should have the knowledge and skills required to effectively design, execute and disseminate your research findings in an impactful way. Additionally, you will have established a network of peer researchers to carry forward as you advance your careers.

restrictions: Restricted to students enrolled in BBiomedSc(Hons); or BSc(Hons) or BAdvSc(Hons) majoring in Biomedical Science only.

Additional timetable information
BIOM6070 runs as an intensive course during Weeks 1 - 5 of the semester.
Students will attend in person for two full days per week (Tuesday and Wednesday), with two blocks of 3 hours (9am to 12 noon and 1pm to 4pm) on each day.
All assessment will be completed within the 5 weeks, except for a Seminar Reflection Report (10%) due in Week 13.

learning_outcomes.description: To understand and apply various software programs for analysis of biomedical literature and data
To create a scientific question and design experiments for testing a hypothesis
To critically evaluate scientific data and previously published work
To communicate research findings through written, oral, poster formats to diverse audiences
To work effectively in a research team, identify the characteristics of effective teamwork and critically evaluate personal and peer contributions to team processes
To evaluate ethical issues in biomedical research and apply culturally inclusive, responsible, and ethical conduct in their research practice

assessment_details.task_description: For this assessment, you are required to complete a workshop diary entry at the end of each workshop throughout the first five weeks of the course. The diary is designed to encourage reflection on your learning, consolidate key concepts, and identify areas for further development. Each week, you will respond to a series of questions related to the workshop topics and learning activities. The workshop diary contributes 25% of your final grade. Your diary will be reviewed weekly by your instructors, with 5% allocated to each week's entry. Assessment will consider the quality of your reflections, your engagement with the workshop activities, and your participation and contribution throughout the course. A failure to reference generative AI or MT use may constitute student misconduct under the Student Code of Conduct . To pass this assessment, students will be required to demonstrate detailed comprehension of their written submission independent of AI and MT tools. learning_activities.topic: Getting to know you and resources for biomedical researchers LEARNING OBJECTIVES: To promote networking and collaboration amongst student cohort To train students to work effectively in teams To be able to conduct scientific research in an ethical, integral, equitable and inclusive manner To understand the opportunities and responsibilities of using AI LEARNING ACTIVITIES: SESSION 1A: Course overview; Honours goal setting and myth busters (with panel of recent honours graduates) SESSION 1B: Introduction to research ethics and ethical use of AI; Cultural Considerations in Research; Generating Graphical Abstracts Learning outcomes: L01, L04, L05, L06

Experimental Design and Research Practices LEARNING OBJECTIVES: To design a scientific question, research hypothesis, experimental aims, and craft an informative abstract To familiarise students with relevant software programs to support biomedical research To familiarise students with scientific communication through poster and oral formats LEARNING ACTIVITIES: SESSION 2B: Introduction to experimental design; Brief introduction/exercise relating to GraphPad Prism, Endnote, and Pubmed; Team activity exploring other useful resources for biomedical researchers SESSION 2B: Art of oral presentations and ECR Showcase. Poster Gallery Walk and Power Hour Learning outcomes: L02, L03, L04, L05, L06

Critical analysis for biomedical scientists LEARNING OBJECTIVES: To critically evaluate scientific data and literature, assessing credibility and reliability To develop skills in formulating and asking questions LEARNING ACTIVITIES: SESSION 3A: Editorial review of selected scientific papers in teams SESSION 3B: EKKA Show Day (no classes) Learning outcomes: L02, L03, L04, L05, L06

Scientific communication and audience targeting LEARNING OBJECTIVES: To develop scientific communication skills using various formats, written, oral, poster To hone skills in presenting to various audiences, including lay To familiarise students in the art of crafting research proposals LEARNING ACTIVITIES: SESSION 4A: Introduction to writing research proposals; Mock assessment of exemplar theses in teams and class discussions SESSION 4B: Tailoring your message to match your audience – group communication task tailoring key messages to diverse audiences (government, community, science peers); Mock Poster presentations and feedback Learning outcomes: L03, L04, L05, L06

Connecting and communicating as biomedical scientists LEARNING OBJECTIVES: To develop SMART skills for research project management To establish an engaging online presence To identify and get the most out of career mentors LEARNING ACTIVITIES: SESSION 5A: Smart skills and soft skills for biomedical researchers; Referee activity; Setting up an engaging LinkedIn or BlueSky account SESSION 5B: Final Poster Presentation Showcase Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04, L05, L06
